title: Maintaining Proper Slope in Gravity Drainage
description: Maintaining correct pitch in horizontal drainage piping is vital for long-term system health. Excess slope can cause liquids to flow ahead of solid waste, leaving debris behind, while insufficient slope leads to low flow velocity, standing water, and sediment accumulation. Proper slope allows liquids and solids to transport together under gravity flow. Regular visual inspection of pipe hangers and structural supports prevents sags or back-pitched sections caused by building settlement, ensuring long-term self-scouring velocity throughout the drain network.

Maintaining Proper Slope in Gravity Drainage

Maintaining correct pitch in horizontal drainage piping is vital for long-term system health. Excess slope can cause liquids to flow ahead of solid waste, leaving debris behind, while insufficient slope leads to low flow velocity, standing water, and sediment accumulation. Proper slope allows liquids and solids to transport together under gravity flow. Regular visual inspection of pipe hangers and structural supports prevents sags or back-pitched sections caused by building settlement, ensuring long-term self-scouring velocity throughout the drain network.
